claims.text: A five-storey building housing college students collapsed on September 6, 2026, in South West Delhi's Satya Niketan area.
At least five people were killed in the Satya Niketan building collapse on September 6, 2026.
Satya Niketan is a dense hub for paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus.
Eleven people were pulled out of the collapsed building in Satya Niketan and taken to the hospital.
Delhi Police stated they are registering an FIR against Anand Bansal, who operates the Hostel Daze paying guest accommodation.
Residents stated that the collapsed Satya Niketan building was at least 50 years old and comprised a basement plus five upper floors.
Repair work was underway in the basement of the Satya Niketan building when the collapse occurred.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial probe into the Satya Niketan building collapse.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi stated that the collapsed building violated building norms, which permitted only a ground floor plus first floor.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi evacuated tenants from an adjoining girls' paying guest building and sealed it.
At least five people were killed and nine rescued after a building housing mostly students collapsed in New Delhi's Satya Niketan area on September 6, 2026.
Around 150 to 200 members of the ABVP student organization protested at Delhi's Civic Centre against the Municipal Corporation of Delhi following the Satya Niketan building collapse.
A security guard was injured when ABVP protesters attempted to forcibly enter the main Civic Centre building in Delhi.
Delhi Police detained around 15 students following the protest at the Civic Centre and initiated proceedings under the Delhi Police Act.
Deputy Commissioner of Police Amit Goel stated that an FIR was registered against building owner Hariram and others at the South Campus police station.
Eyewitnesses told local media that up to 50 people were inside the five-storey building in Satya Niketan when it collapsed at around 13:30 local time on Sunday.
A local shop owner stated that the building leaseholder was conducting excavation work in the basement to expand the hostel.
More than 1,000 building collapses have been recorded in Delhi over the past three years according to fire department figures.
Eleven people were killed in April when a residential building collapsed in north-eastern Delhi.
ISRO rejected reports suggesting it will be privatised or its role diminished, calling such assertions baseless and incorrect.
IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka stated that ISRO will remain the bedrock of the Indian space sector and lead next-generation space programmes.
IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka stated that India has set a target of achieving 50 space launches a year by 2030.
India currently has over 450 space startups, compared to a handful five years ago.
Indian private company Skyroot successfully launched its Vikram-1 rocket into orbit on July 18.

Nine ISRO employee associations sent a joint letter dated September 4 to ISRO Chairperson V. Narayanan seeking official clarification on plans to transfer manufacturing and operations to private entities.
The ISRO employee associations cited public remarks made on August 21 by IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka stating that ISRO would eventually not manufacture launch vehicles.
India aims to grow its space economy from approximately $8.4 billion to $44 billion by 2033.
Employees of India's Department of Space are exempted from the statutory definition of industry and are organized as service associations rather than trade unions.
ISRO launched its EOS-05 Earth imaging satellite aboard the GSLV-F17 from Sriharikota on September 4.
ISRO employee associations stated in their letter that a policy reducing ISRO to a residual R&D boutique while launch vehicle production passes out of public hands cannot be accepted without debate.
India's space goals include establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and conducting an Indian crewed mission to the Moon by 2040.
ISRO stated that strategic and nationally critical capabilities will continue to be governed by security, safety, quality, and national-interest considerations under government ownership.
The letter to ISRO leadership was signed by employee associations from centres including the ISRO Staff Association, SHAR Employees Association, and ISAC Employees Association.
